wars.name: Vadda Ghalughara
wars.outcome: 5 February 1762 at Kup-Rahira (Ludhiana district): the Durrani and allies surprise the Sikhs; the Harmandir Sahib is blown up on 10 April 1762; the Sikhs recover, win at Harnaulgarh, take payment from Zain Khan in May, and are 'victorious in the 17 October 1762'.
wars.note: No ground changed hands in 1762 on the page; the Sikhs raided the Lahore region and Jalandhar Doab in July-August.

wars.name: Zaman Shah's invasion of the Punjab
wars.outcome: 'Zaman Shah Durrani invaded Punjab, but was forced to retreat' (1797-98); Ranjit Singh then took Lahore, 'confirmed on the possession of Lahore by the Durrani ruler, Zaman Shah'.

wars.outcome: 'In 1799, Ranjit Singh of the Sukerchakia Misl captured Lahore from the Sikh triumvirate'; the start of the Sikh Empire and the end of the confederacy.

notes: Budget: 5 pages, all used. Cliopatria rows: 'Sikh Confederacy' 1762-1806 (7 shapes, 1763-1768 missing). The Misl page gives the confederacy as 1748-1799, so the dossier starts in 1748 (core at Amritsar, new keyframe, low confidence) and ends in 1799; Cliopatria's 1800-1806 shapes (5,631 and 3,082 km2) are remnant misls, not the confederacy, and are kept as 'adjust'/'ok' with the status change. The Sikh Empire dossier (sa-05-f) records gains from 'sikh-confederacy' in 1800 (the Punjab core) and 1802 (Amritsar); this dossier hands the core over in its 1799 dissolve and names the Amritsar remnant 'bhangi-misl'. The Cliopatria shape is a set of city patches (Lahore, Amritsar, Kasur, Gujrat, Sialkot, Gujranwala, Jullundur, Ludhiana), 57,000 km2 by cells, none in Haryana and none at Multan or Rawalpindi; the Cis-Sutlej Sikh states (the Phulkian misl) are missing and are added from 1764. No page opened dates the Sukerchakia, Kanhaiya, Ahluwalia, Ramgarhia, Nakai or Dallewalia lands, so the detail of 1772-1798 is unverified. The Misl page gives no area, capital or ruler list; no ruler strip. Not on any page opened: who held Lahore before 1765 (counterpart durrani-empire is an inference, confidence 2); from whom Kasur was taken in 1761; the Multan conquest of 1772 (Bhangi page silent); Ahmad Shah Durrani's invasions of 1764-1767. The Misl page does not date the Dal Khalsa to 1748 (it gives 1733-1735) and gives the 29 March 1748 date on Dilgeer's account. Counterparts needing dossiers: bhangi-misl (1748-1810, capital Amritsar; Lahore 1765-1799), sukerchakia-misl (Ranjit Singh's misl, Gujranwala; sa-05-f's sikh-empire names it as a predecessor), the Phulkian states (Patiala, 1763). Gazetteer: no place entries for Sirhind, Ferozepur, Jhelum, Attock or Kangra; regions Majha, Doaba and Cis-Sutlej are absent (circles round Patiala, Ambala and Karnal are used for the Sirhind country). [Reviewer sa-05-e, 2026-10-25] Keyframes sikh-confederacy_1800, _1803 and _1806 set to verdict 'wrong' (shapes after the 1799 end belong to remnant misls), following the convention for post-dissolution shapes.
